articles.summary: Conflicting court rulings Tuesday left Missouri's congressional map in legal limbo less than two months before the November general election, with litigation continuing over which districts will govern the state's races. Earlier Tuesday, Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh denied Missouri’s emergency appeal seeking to revive the state's revised Republican-backed congressional map, leaving in place the Missouri Supreme Court's ruling blocking the map from being used in November. Kavanaugh acted alone and did not refer the application to the full Supreme Court. Later Tuesday, however, Chief U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark issued a 14-day temporary restraining order directing Missouri officials to use the revised congressional map while the federal case proceeds, setting up competing court orders over which districts should govern the November election. The Missouri Supreme Court had ruled last week that the revised map never legally took effect because a voter-backed referendum petition suspended the law pending a statewide vote, leaving the congressional districts adopted in 2022 in place for the November election. articles.summary: YouTube/MissAmerica/Getty Images The new Miss America winner made history by becoming the first Miss Texas to win the competition in over 50 years—and the first Black woman ever crowned wearing her natural curl texture. On Sunday, Sept. 6, Regan Hutsell was crowned Miss America 2027 in West Palm Beach, Florida. She previously won the titles of Miss Houston in September 2025 and Miss Texas in June. The 25-year-old beauty queen is a trained ballet dancer and became a Radio City Rockette at 18 before traveling through Europe with the Birmingham Royal Ballet. She has won multiple gold medals for her talent and also won an award for her jazz dance performance during the pageant competition. Read more at The Daily Beast.
